title: Numerical inverse problems and regularization error

items.title: Tikhonov error separates bias, data noise, discretization and solve residual
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces, let
$A:X\to Y$ be compact (hence bounded), and let $A_h:X\to Y$ be a bounded
discrete operator whose range is a finite-dimensional subspace of $Y$. For
$\lambda>0$,
define

$$R_\lambda=(A^*A+\lambda I_X)^{-1}A^*,\qquad R_{\lambda,h}=(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I_X)^{-1}A_h^*.$$

These maps are well-defined by [[lem-hilbert-tikhonov-normal-operator-invertible]]. Let $x^\dagger\in X$, $y=Ax^\dagger$, $y_\delta=y+e$ with $\|e\|\le\delta$ and $\delta\ge0$, and let $\widetilde x\in X$. Define the exact discrete normal-equation residual

$$r_h=(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I_X)\widetilde x-A_h^*y_\delta.$$

Then the following chain is exact:

$$x^\dagger-\widetilde x=(x^\dagger-R_\lambda y) +(R_\lambda y-R_\lambda y_\delta) +(R_\lambda y_\delta-R_{\lambda,h}y_\delta) +(R_{\lambda,h}y_\delta-\widetilde x).$$

Its norm satisfies

$$\|x^\dagger-\widetilde x\|\le \|x^\dagger-R_\lambda y\|+\frac{\delta}{2\sqrt\lambda} +\|(R_\lambda-R_{\lambda,h})y_\delta\|+\frac{\|r_h\|}{\lambda}.$$

The first term is regularization bias, the second is data noise, the third is the regularized-operator discretization difference, and the fourth is the solve residual. The third term receives a numerical bound only when an operator-perturbation bound is supplied: if $\|R_\lambda-R_{\lambda,h}\|\le\eta_{\lambda,h}$, it is at most $\eta_{\lambda,h}\|y_\delta\|$. If residual evaluation returns $\widehat r_h$ with a certified $\|r_h-\widehat r_h\|\le\rho_h$, the last term is at most $(\|\widehat r_h\|+\rho_h)/\lambda$. If an algorithm has a specified exact-arithmetic stopping output $x_{\mathrm{stop}}$ and returns a computed output $\widetilde x$, the last difference can further split as

$$R_{\lambda,h}y_\delta-\widetilde x= (R_{\lambda,h}y_\delta-x_{\mathrm{stop}}) +(x_{\mathrm{stop}}-\widetilde x).$$

Writing $r_{\mathrm{stop}}=(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I_X)x_{\mathrm{stop}} -A_h^*y_\delta$, the first term is at most $\|r_{\mathrm{stop}}\|/\lambda$; the second is the separate returned-output roundoff term. Any bound on that roundoff or on residual-evaluation error requires its own arithmetic hypotheses. For a discretized datum $y_{h,\delta}=A_hx^\dagger+e$ formed before inversion, put $d_h=(A-A_h)x^\dagger=y_\delta-y_{h,\delta}$. Let $\widetilde x_h\in X$ be a computed discrete output. The corresponding exact refinement is

$$x^\dagger-\widetilde x_h=(x^\dagger-R_\lambda y) +(R_\lambda y-R_\lambda y_\delta) +R_\lambda d_h+(R_\lambda-R_{\lambda,h})y_{h,\delta} +(R_{\lambda,h}y_{h,\delta}-\widetilde x_h),$$

so the forward residual discarded by quadrature or collocation is counted before inversion as $R_\lambda d_h$, with $\|R_\lambda d_h\|\le\|d_h\|/(2\sqrt\lambda)$. The separate operator discretization and solve terms remain. For this refined chain, define $r_{h,h}=(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I_X)\widetilde x_h-A_h^*y_{h,\delta}$; then $\|R_{\lambda,h}y_{h,\delta}-\widetilde x_h\|\le\|r_{h,h}\|/\lambda$. If its evaluation returns $\widehat r_{h,h}$ with a certified $\|r_{h,h}-\widehat r_{h,h}\|\le\rho_{h,h}$, the last term is at most $(\|\widehat r_{h,h}\|+\rho_{h,h})/\lambda$. No rate for $d_h$, no operator perturbation estimate, and no floating-point residual bound is implicit. When $X,Y$ are finite-dimensional and $b=Ax^\dagger+e$, the same identity is the canonical Tikhonov bias/noise formula

$$x^\dagger-A^\#_\lambda b=(I-A^\#_\lambda A)x^\dagger-A^\#_\lambda e, \qquad A^\#_\lambda=(A^*A+\lambda I)^{-1}A^*.$$

Here $\lambda$ is the coefficient of $\|x\|^2$ in
$\|Ax-b\|^2+\lambda\|x\|^2$.

For stored finite matrices, [[lem-computed-augmented-tikhonov-solve-residual-and-output-error]] supplies the concrete augmented-QR or independently certified-residual application: take its $\rho$ as $\rho_h$ with datum $y_\delta$, or as $\rho_{h,h}$ with datum $y_{h,\delta}$. It bounds returned-output roundoff for the exact direct-solve target and retains explicit real/complex realization, square-root representation, successful-operation and nonsingularity conditions.
items.strategy:
1.1 By [F7], $A$ is bounded, and [F8] supplies the Hilbert-space hypotheses. By [F1], both shifted normal operators are invertible, so the displayed $R_\lambda$ and $R_{\lambda,h}$ are defined. Multiplying their definitions by their normal operators gives $(A^*A+\lambda I)R_\lambda=A^*$ and $(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I)R_{\lambda,h}=A_h^*$. [given, A1, F1, F3, F7, F8, algebra]

1.2 Adding and subtracting the intermediate vectors $R_\lambda y$, $R_\lambda y_\delta$, and $R_{\lambda,h}y_\delta$ cancels the intervening terms and proves the stated four-term identity. Since $y_\delta=y+e$, [F2] gives $\|R_\lambda y-R_\lambda y_\delta\|=\|R_\lambda e\| \le\delta/(2\sqrt\lambda)$. [given, F2, algebra]

1.3 Adding and subtracting $x_{\mathrm{stop}}$ gives the optional stopping/roundoff identity. The normal equation for $R_{\lambda,h}y_\delta$ and the definition of $r_{\mathrm{stop}}$ imply $(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I)(x_{\mathrm{stop}}-R_{\lambda,h}y_\delta) =r_{\mathrm{stop}}$. By [F1], the stopping term is at most $\|r_{\mathrm{stop}}\|/\lambda$; the other term is exactly the stated roundoff difference. [given, F1, algebra]

1.4 In the refined datum case, $y_\delta-y_{h,\delta}=(Ax^\dagger+e)-(A_hx^\dagger+e)=d_h$. Inserting $R_\lambda y_{h,\delta}$ and $R_{\lambda,h}y_{h,\delta}$ into the chain therefore gives the displayed five-term identity by cancellation. [given, F3, algebra]

2.1 Let $z=R_{\lambda,h}y_\delta$. The normal equation in step 1.1 gives $(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I)(\widetilde x-z)=r_h$. By [F1], $\|\widetilde x-z\|\le\|r_h\|/\lambda$. The triangle inequality [F9] applied to the four-term identity, using step 1.2 for its noise term, proves the stated total error bound. [F1, F9, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 Applying [F2] to $d_h$ bounds its pre-inversion contribution by $\|R_\lambda d_h\|\le\|d_h\|/(2\sqrt\lambda)$. Applying [F1] to $r_{h,h}=(A_h^*A_h+\lambda I)(\widetilde x_h-R_{\lambda,h}y_{h,\delta})$ gives the stated refined solve-residual bound. Under the residual-evaluation hypothesis, the triangle inequality [F9] gives $\|r_{h,h}\|\le\|\widehat r_{h,h}\|+\rho_{h,h}$. [F1, F2, F9, step 1.4, algebra]

3.1 By [F4], an assumed operator-norm bound $\|R_\lambda-R_{\lambda,h}\|\le\eta_{\lambda,h}$ gives $\|(R_\lambda-R_{\lambda,h})y_\delta\| \le\eta_{\lambda,h}\|y_\delta\|$. Also, the triangle inequality [F9] gives $\|r_h\|\le\|\widehat r_h\|+\|r_h-\widehat r_h\| \le\|\widehat r_h\|+\rho_h$ under the stated residual-evaluation hypothesis. These are conditional estimates, not automatic stability claims. [given, F4, F9, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 In the finite-matrix case with $A_h=A$ and the exact regularized output $\widetilde x=R_\lambda y_\delta$, [F5]–[F6] identify $R_\lambda$ with the canonical Tikhonov minimizer. The baseline identity from step 1.2 then reduces to the displayed finite-matrix bias/noise formula. [F5, F6, step 1.2, algebra]

4.2 For stored finite data, or for supplied isometric coordinates $A_h=VMU^*$ and returned output $U\widehat x$, apply [F10] to the coefficient matrix $M$ (the matrix case uses identity embeddings) and datum $g=y_\delta$ or $g=y_{h,\delta}$. The exact normal residual lifts isometrically to $r_h$ or $r_{h,h}$, with any certified coordinate-data and orthogonal-output allowances from [F10]. Hence steps 2.2 and 3.1 apply. For the exact direct augmented solve, $x_{\mathrm{stop}}=R_{\lambda,h}g$, and [F10] bounds the returned-output term by $(\|\widehat r\|+\rho)/\lambda$. The analytic identity and its independent bias, noise and discretization terms are unchanged. [F10, step 1.3, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Computed augmented Tikhonov solves have certified residual and output-error bounds
items.statement:
Let stored $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$ and $y\in\mathbb F^m$ be real or complex, $m,n\ge1$, and let stored real $\lambda>0$. Let $x_\lambda=(A^*A+\lambda I)^{-1}A^*y$. Compute $\alpha=\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt\lambda)>0$ under the successful normal-range square-root model, and solve the stored augmented problem $\min_x\|[A;\alpha I]x-[y;0]\|_2$ by scaled Householder QR and rounded substitution. For complex inputs use the realification described below, so the backend uses only real triangular divisions. Every operation must succeed; failed pivots, invalid operations and out-of-range nonzero intermediates return range-failure.

For any returned $\widehat x$, evaluate $\widehat r$ and its certified allowance $\rho$ by [[lem-rounded-linear-and-normal-residual-certificates]] for the intended residual $r=(A^*A+\lambda I)\widehat x-A^*y$. Then
$$\|\widehat x-x_\lambda\|_2\le\frac{\|\widehat r\|_2+\rho}{\lambda}.$$
This bounds returned-output roundoff relative to the exact direct-solve target $x_{\rm stop}=x_\lambda$. It also certifies the solve term in any larger analytic error chain, irrespective of the backend. The representation of $\sqrt\lambda$ contributes no hidden change of target: $|\alpha^2-\lambda|\le(2u+u^2)\lambda$. If residual evaluation instead uses exact $\alpha^2$, add $|\alpha^2-\lambda|\|\widehat x\|_2$ to its allowance; rounding a computed $\alpha^2$ needs its own scalar error as well.

The backend's nearby least-squares conclusion holds under the completed QR/solve hypotheses and nonsingularity condition. In real dimension, write $C=[A;\alpha I]$ and $\epsilon_Q=\beta_Q\|C\|_F$. A sufficient check is $\epsilon_Q<\alpha$ and $\|\Delta R\|_F<\alpha-\epsilon_Q$. An explicit certified nonsingularity check may replace this sufficient margin.

For a Hilbert-space discrete operator, supply isometries $U:\mathbb F^n\to X$ and $V:\mathbb F^m\to Y$ with $A_h=VAU^*$, and return $U\widehat x$. With coefficient datum $y_c=V^*y_\delta$, the exact normal solution lies in $\operatorname{ran}U$ and the coefficient residual lifts isometrically, so the same certificate applies to $r_h$; likewise use $V^*y_{h,\delta}$ for $r_{h,h}$. If a stored coefficient datum $\widehat y_c$ differs from $V^*y$ by at most $\epsilon_y$, add $\|A\|_2\epsilon_y$ to the residual allowance. If the returned output also has an orthogonal component $z\perp\operatorname{ran}U$ of norm at most $\epsilon_\perp$, add $\lambda\epsilon_\perp$. Finite rank alone does not supply these coordinate or output certificates.
items.strategy:
1.1 The stored augmented matrix has full column rank, since $\|[A;\alpha I]z\|_2^2=\|Az\|_2^2+\alpha^2\|z\|_2^2\ge\alpha^2\|z\|_2^2$. If $C+\Delta_Q=\widehat Q\widehat R$, then $\|\widehat Rz\|=\|(C+\Delta_Q)z\|\ge(\alpha-\epsilon_Q)\|z\|$. Under the sufficient margin, the further triangular perturbation preserves a positive lower bound. Thus the nonsingularity premise in [F2] holds under the stated check. The theorem still explicitly requires successful arithmetic; exact full rank alone does not ensure rounded success. [given, F2, algebra]

1.2 For complex inputs identify $z=z_R+iz_I$ with $(z_R,z_I)\in\mathbb R^{2n}$. The real matrix $A_R=\begin{pmatrix}\operatorname{Re}A&-\operatorname{Im}A\\\operatorname{Im}A&\operatorname{Re}A\end{pmatrix}$ represents exactly the same linear map, preserves vector norms, and satisfies $\|A_R\|_2=\|A\|_2$, $\|A_R\|_F=\sqrt2\|A\|_F$ by direct component sums. Apply [F2] to $[A_R;\alpha I_{2n}]$ and datum $((\operatorname{Re}y,\operatorname{Im}y),0)$; this is exactly the original complex objective. Mapping its output back needs only component pairing, so introduces no arithmetic error or unmodeled complex division. [F2, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 By [F3], $\alpha=\sqrt\lambda(1+\delta)$, $|\delta|\le u$, whence $|\alpha^2-\lambda|\le(2u+u^2)\lambda$. For any $z$, Cauchy-Schwarz gives $\|(A^*A+\lambda I)z\|\|z\|\ge\langle(A^*A+\lambda I)z,z\rangle=\|Az\|^2+\lambda\|z\|^2\ge\lambda\|z\|^2$. The normal equation [F4] therefore implies $\|\widehat x-x_\lambda\|\le\|r\|/\lambda\le(\|\widehat r\|+\rho)/\lambda$ by [F1]. Replacing the coefficient in a residual by $\alpha^2$ changes that exact residual by $(\alpha^2-\lambda)\widehat x$, giving the stated additional allowance. [F1, F3, F4, algebra]

2.2 In exact arithmetic with the intended $\sqrt\lambda$, full-rank augmented QR returns the unique minimizer in [F4], hence $x_{\rm stop}=x_\lambda$. Step 2.1 bounds the returned computed output's difference from that target, including square-root representation and all solve error through its certified residual. For an iterative stopping target different from $x_\lambda$, retain separate stopping and output terms rather than calling their sum pure roundoff. [F2, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

3.1 In the supplied Hilbert representation, $U^*U=I$, $V^*V=I$, and $A_h^*=UA^*V^*$. The subspaces $\operatorname{ran}U$ and its orthogonal complement are invariant under $A_h^*A_h+\lambda I$; on the complement that operator is $\lambda I$ and its right-hand side $A_h^*y$ has zero component. Thus the exact normal solution is $Ux_\lambda$, with coefficient datum $V^*y$. Direct substitution gives $r_h=U((A^*A+\lambda I)\widehat x-A^*V^*y)$, and isometry preserves its norm. Perturbing the datum adds $UA^*(\widehat y_c-V^*y)$ of norm at most $\|A\|\epsilon_y$; an orthogonal output component adds $\lambda z$. Triangle inequality gives the stated allowances. These explicit coordinate hypotheses preserve the general Hilbert theorem while justifying its concrete finite solve. [step 2.1, algebra] ∎
